hero.title: Toll Brothers Homebuying AI Chatbot
hero.subtitle: Designing context-awareness, category recommendations, and home comparison

sections.intro: I led design for Toll Brothers' first AI chatbot and shaped three features. The core context slot system allows the user to build up homebuying criteria (location, price, beds, etc.) with suggested prompts. The category cards with nested product recommendations surfaces key marketing terms. The comparison feature leverages AI capbilities to summarize qualitative and quantitative differences between home choices. The context system and category cards were approved for implementation by internal stakeholders. The comparison feature was scoped for a future release.

frames.text:
Researching UX for AI chatbots presents a unique challenge since chatbot experiences can swing wildly depending on user queries. I indexed 8 commercial chatbots, and evaluated the responses for an average query (or suggested prompts) and follow-up. Baseline features include custom UI for:

- Starting prompts
- Smart categorization
- Product recommendation
- Follow-up suggestions

Notable differentiators came mainly from Amazon, Sephora, and Kayak. These included:

- Shopping companion with main site
- Manual refinement controls
- Multi-context awareness and persistent memory
- Comparison charts

Working with the creative director, I shaped three initial feature requirements. The first requirement followed baseline conventions and using distinct UI for suggested prompts and product recommendations. The second requirement is a context slot system specific for homebuying. I identified location, timeframe, price, size, and amenities as key factors. The initial flow should use suggested prompts to encourage users to provide location as a requirement and fill in at least one other slot for refinement. Taking inspiration from Amazon, I shaped the third requirement to wrap product suggestions in categories. In the homebuying context, Toll Brothers offers product types like Active Adult (55+) that need some explanation beyond a product's data. Categories serve three purposes:

- Surface marketing terms.
- Reflect the user's initial contexts by showing categories only relevant to those slots.
- Invite users to fill in another context slot through their behavior.

sections.intro: After demonstrating the initial flow, the development team questioned whether the context slot system was necessary for the MVP build since the business goal was to collect data on user queries. I argued that context retention and flexible query interpretations elevate the chatbot from a simple filtered search. Demonstrating the chatbot working with ideal queries helps build trust in the AI's capabilities and encourages users to ask more specific questions, which is the initial business goal. I pointed to Amazon and Kayak as example chatbots with the most developed features, and both scaffold conversations with suggested prompts to encourage continued engagement. The team agreed, and the initial flow was scoped into the MVP build.

frames.text: Once the flow drilled down into the product itself, the UX opened up, and I had room to explore new feature ideas. Amazon and Sephora use a radical UX approach of turning the chatbot into a side-by-side companion with the main site. That specific pattern was discussed as too disruptive to the current site, but it raised an interesting question of how to leverage AI to provide value beyond the main site. Currently, the main site lacks a dedicated product comparison feature (other than showing product cards side-by-side). AI is uniquely good at summarizing differences between two objects. I designed a recommendation feature that suggested product comparison prompts and presented the information in a dedicated UI. The UX team agreed that this feature offered unique value and scoped it for a future release.
